title: Use duckdb formatting settings
body:
Copied the `.clang-format` from duckdb and ran `make format`
(motivation is that I'm updating the repo in preparation for duckdb v1.3 and I wanted to reduce the visual noise of not having formatting I'm used to)

This formatting makes it easier to read the code and as a result - easier to work with.
author: Tishj

title: Incorrect Avro container file magic number
body:
Hi, thank you for providing this extension :) 

I tried to use it today on an avro file that is stored in AWS S3 and contains messages from a Kafka topic.

```sql
select * from read_avro('s3://bucket/messages.avro');
```

This results in the following error message:

```
Invalid Input Error:
Incorrect Avro container file magic number
```

I am not sure whether this is related to the limitations mentioned in the README.md, but thought I ask here regardless.
author: migarstka

comments.body: Does this file use the Avro container format? Can you read it with e.g. pyavro?

Hi @hannes,

You are right. My file seems to be corrupted for some reason.

I tried again with an avro file that I generated myself and it works without issues.


```sql
load avro;
select * from read_avro('users.avro');
```


Python script to generate valid file (in case anyone else needs it):

```python
import json
from avro.schema import parse
import avro.datafile
import avro.io
import io
import random

# Define the Avro schema
schema_json = {
    "namespace": "example.avro",
    "type": "record",
    "name": "User",
    "fields": [
        {"name": "id", "type": "int"},
        {"name": "name", "type": "string"},
        {"name": "age", "type": "int"},
        {"name": "email", "type": "string"},
        {"name": "active", "type": "boolean"}
    ]
}

# Convert the schema to a string and parse it
schema_str = json.dumps(schema_json)
schema = parse(schema_str)

# Create sample data
sample_data = []
first_names = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "Eva", "Frank", "Grace", "Henry", "Ivy", "Jack"]
last_names = ["Smith", "Johnson", "Williams", "Brown", "Jones", "Miller", "Davis", "Garcia", "Wilson", "Martinez"]

for i in range(10):
    sample_data.append({
        "id": i+1,
        "name": f"{random.choice(first_names)} {random.choice(last_names)}",
        "age": random.randint(18, 65),
        "email": f"user{i+1}@example.com",
        "active": random.choice([True, False])
    })

# Write the data to an Avro file
file_path = "users.avro"
with open(file_path, "wb") as out:
    writer = avro.datafile.DataFileWriter(out, avro.io.DatumWriter(), schema)
    for record in sample_data:
        writer.append(record)
    writer.close()
```
